dedupe_keys.name: uscg navcen gps constellation status and notice advisories to navstar users nanus

description: The US Coast Guard Navigation Center publishes the current status of the GPS constellation as a table with, for each satellite, its orbital plane and slot, space vehicle number (SVN), pseudo-random noise code (PRN), block type (such as IIR, IIR-M, IIF and III), clock in use, and the latest Notice Advisory to Navstar Users (NANU) with its type, such as a forecast outage (FCSTDV) or outage summary (FCSTSUMM), start date and subject. A slant chart shows plane and slot assignments. NANUs announce planned maintenance, unplanned outages and satellite decommissioning, and NAVCEN keeps them as a searchable archive. Coverage: the whole GPS constellation, about 31 satellites, current status with NANU history. Format and access: web tables and NANU text messages, free. Caveats: plane and slot are no longer given in operational advisories since a 2018 interface change, so the chart is kept by hand; status of a satellite is not the signal quality a user sees. Simulation uses: satellite outages and constellation changes as inputs to GNSS availability and timing resilience scenarios. This record answers the GPS.gov applications and status item: the gps.gov status page moved and NAVCEN is its data source. Related records: data-navcen-gps-problem-reports-guide gives user reports of GPS problems; case_study-gps-utc-offset-anomaly-january-2016 describes a constellation-wide timing error; data-igs-gnss-products gives orbits and clocks.
